title: Account Reconciliation Automation: What It Is and How to Do It
summary: What account reconciliation automation is, the levels from rules to AI agents, how to automate reconciliation step by step, what to automate first, and the pitfalls.
body_markdown:
Account reconciliation is the most repetitive job in the close: matching the general ledger against the bank, the subledgers, and other sources, line by line, then documenting and signing off on every account. It is slow, error-prone, and it scales badly. **Account reconciliation automation** replaces that grind, using software to match transactions, clear what agrees, and surface only the exceptions that need a person.


This guide explains what account reconciliation automation is, the levels of automation from rules to AI agents, how to automate account reconciliation step by step, what to automate first, and the pitfalls to avoid.


## **What is account reconciliation automation?**


Account reconciliation automation is the use of software to perform reconciliation work that was done by hand: matching transactions between two sets of records, clearing the items that agree, flagging or resolving the ones that do not, and producing the documentation and sign-off that make the account defensible. It ranges from simple rules-based matching to AI and autonomous agents that reconcile accounts end to end, with a human approving.


> Automation does not remove reconciliation; it changes who does the matching. Instead of a person clearing hundreds of items to find the few that are wrong, the software clears the matches and the person reviews only what is left.


## **What account reconciliation automation replaces**


To see where automation helps, it helps to name the manual steps it takes over:


- **Pulling the data.** Exporting balances and transactions from the ERP, bank, and subledgers into spreadsheets.
- **Matching line by line.** Comparing one record against another to find what agrees and what does not.
- **Chasing exceptions.** Investigating the handful of items that do not tie, across timing, format, and missing entries.
- **Documenting.** Attaching support and writing up explanations for each account.
- **Reviewing and signing off.** Routing each reconciliation for review and certification.


Automation can take on all five to different degrees. The matching and documentation are the easiest to automate; the judgment on genuine exceptions is where a human stays in the loop.


## **The levels of reconciliation automation**


Not all automation is equal. It is useful to think of it as a ladder, because most teams are somewhere in the middle and the gap at the top is where the biggest gains are:


Level What it does Human role


Manual Match line by line in spreadsheets Does everything


Rules-based automation Auto-matches exact, rule-defined items Resolves every exception


AI reconciliation Matches imperfect, equivalent records and investigates exceptions Reviews and approves


Agentic Runs the whole workflow across systems and drafts entries Approves at the gates


Most reconciliation tools stop at rules-based matching: they clear the clean items and leave the rest in an exceptions queue.[AI reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/ai-reconciliation) works that queue too, and the agentic level runs the entire workflow. The further up the ladder, the less is left for a person to do by hand.


## **How to automate account reconciliation**


Automating reconciliation is less a single project than a sequence. A path that works:


- **1. Connect your data.** Link the ERP, bank feeds, and subledgers so balances and transactions flow in automatically instead of being exported by hand.
- **2. Standardize the reconciliation.** Define what matches what, the tolerances, and the frequency, so the rules and the AI have a clear target.
- **3. Automate the clean matches first.** Turn on rules-based auto-matching for the high-volume, well-structured items (most bank and transaction matching).
- **4. Layer AI on the exceptions.** Add AI that matches imperfect, equivalent records and investigates the discrepancies the rules leave behind.
- **5. Automate the documentation.** Let the system assemble support and the audit trail so every match and adjustment ties back to source.
- **6. Keep a human approving.** Route the finished reconciliations for review and sign-off; automation does the work, people own the judgment and the controls.
- **7. Move from batch to continuous.** Once it runs reliably, reconcile throughout the period instead of all at month-end. See[continuous accounting](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/continuous-accounting) .


## **What to automate first**


Start where volume is high and the data is structured, then move to the harder reconciliations:


- **Bank reconciliation.** High volume and relatively clean, the best first win. See[automating bank reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/automate-bank-reconciliation) .
- **High-volume transaction matching.** Payments, invoices, and receipts matched across systems.
- **Balance sheet account reconciliations.** Tying each balance-sheet account to its support at period-end. See[balance sheet reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/balance-sheet-reconciliation) .
- **Intercompany reconciliation.** Matching activity between entities before consolidation. See[intercompany reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/intercompany-reconciliation) .


## **Benefits of automating account reconciliation**


- **Faster close.** Reconciliations that took days run in minutes or continuously, compressing the[financial close](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/financial-close-automation) .
- **Fewer exceptions to touch.** Automation clears the matches and, with AI, the near-misses, shrinking the manual queue.
- **Higher accuracy.** Consistent matching catches errors, duplicates, and fraud that manual review misses.
- **Scales without headcount.** Transaction volume can grow without adding reconcilers.
- **Audit-ready by default.** Every match and adjustment traces back to source, so the account is defensible.


## **Pitfalls to watch**


- **Messy source data.** Rules-based tools break on format and timing differences; this is exactly where AI matching earns its place.
- **The exceptions ceiling.** Rules clear the easy items and stop; if most of your time goes to exceptions, rules alone will not move the needle.
- **Weak traceability.** Automation without an audit trail trades speed for risk. Insist that every match ties back to source.
- **Over-trusting the output.** Automation should do the work, not own the judgment. Keep a human approving the results and the controls.

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is account reconciliation automation?**


Account reconciliation automation is the use of software to match transactions between records, clear what agrees, resolve or flag what does not, and produce the documentation and sign-off for each account. It spans rules-based matching, AI, and autonomous agents that reconcile accounts end to end with a human approving.


### **How do you automate account reconciliation?**


Connect your ERP, bank, and subledger data; standardize what matches what; automate the clean, high-volume matches with rules; layer AI on the exceptions; automate the documentation and audit trail; and keep a human approving. Over time, shift from a month-end batch to continuous reconciliation.


### **What part of reconciliation can be automated?**


The matching, exception investigation, and documentation can be automated to a high degree, especially for bank, transaction, and balance-sheet reconciliations. The judgment on genuine discrepancies and the final sign-off stay with a person, which is what keeps the account defensible.


### **Is automated reconciliation accurate and auditable?**


Yes, when it is built with traceability. The best automation ties every match and adjustment back to source records and keeps a human approving, so the work is both consistent and defensible to an auditor. Accuracy comes from consistent matching plus review at the gates.


### **What is the difference between automated and AI reconciliation?**


Traditional automated reconciliation uses fixed rules and only matches records that line up exactly, leaving the rest for a person.[AI reconciliation](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/ai-reconciliation) matches imperfect, equivalent records and investigates the exceptions, so far less is left for manual work. AI is the more capable tier of reconciliation automation.


## **The bottom line**


Account reconciliation automation takes the most repetitive job in the close and hands the matching and documentation to software, so people review rather than investigate from scratch. The levels run from rules-based matching to AI to autonomous agents, and the gains grow the further up you go, from a faster close to reconciliation that runs continuously and scales without headcount.
